messages:
alice: quick heads-up — running into weird bursts when prefetch is on and transport falls back. python client prefetches next chunk, then transport failover retriggers the same request => double work and higher qps.
ben: can you paste a trimmed log? is the retry happening client-side or server-side?
alice: pasted logs below

```
[2024-07-02T16:10:01Z] client: prefetch(next_token=abc123) -> sent to http
[2024-07-02T16:10:01Z] transport: http->timeout
[2024-07-02T16:10:01Z] client: retry(policy=hedged) -> sent to grpc
[2024-07-02T16:10:02Z] server: processed request token=abc123 (first time)
[2024-07-02T16:10:02Z] server: processed request token=abc123 (second time)
```
carla: sounds like invocations are idempotent in theory but we don't have de-dupe at routing. also prefetch triggers before previous completes.
dan: what's the prefetch trigger in the SDKs? time-based or count-based?
alice: python/ts use a simple window: when in-flight < prefetch_max_inflight and remaining_tokens > 0 we fire the next page. grace_ms is 50ms by default. go uses conservative single prefetch.
eva: ok tradeoffs: keep aggressive prefetch (lower latency) vs avoid duplicate work on failover. transports can fail fast -> fallbacks amplify hedging.
ben: options we should consider:
- A) Add lightweight client-side reservation token: before prefetch send a cheap "reserve" to route; transport responds OK, then client sends full request. Pros: avoids duplicate work on failover. Cons: extra RTT and complexity.
- B) Align retry/backoff windows across transports: ensure if http times out and grpc is tried we delay hedging by jitter tuned to prefetch grace_ms. Pros: low complexity. Cons: brittle tuning cross langs.
- C) Idempotency + server de-dupe: add idempotency seq on prefetch requests and server-side de-dupe. Pros: robust. Cons: needs backend change + state.
- D) Cancel-on-handshake: when transport signals failover, send cancel to previous inflight prefetch. Pros: immediate. Cons: depends on transport cancellation semantics (gRPC ok, HTTP not always).
carla: leaning C long term, B short term. C requires route metadata and storage TTL for de-dupe keys.
dan: any compatibility pitfalls for Python/TS/Go? we need the same prefetch policy surface and a minimal contract for idempotency keys if we go C.
eva: propose incremental plan:
1) short-term: implement B across SDKs — add jittered delay before second-transport hedged retry and increase default grace_ms to 100ms for python/ts (go keep 1). add telemetry to flag duplicates.
2) mid-term: prototype C for one route (embeddings/paged-generation) with server de-dupe and legacy toggle.
3) long-term: RFC for reservation API + transport handshake improvements (A + D combined) for dedicated/private flows.

alice: quick config sketch for B (python/ts):
```yaml
prefetch:
  enabled: true
  max_inflight: 2
  grace_ms: 100
retry:
  hedged_delay_multiplier: 1.5
  transport_fallback: jittered
telemetry:
  duplicate_request_metric: true
```
ben: add tests:
- simulate http timeout + grpc retry and assert duplicate_request_metric increments
- assert latency improvement doesn't regress beyond 5% for common workloads
carla: I'll own the telemetry and tests for TS. dan you ok to patch go to keep conservative prefetch and emit metric?
dan: yes, i'll add a flag in go client to opt into the new grace_ms and wire metrics.
alice: I'll open a short RFC with the proposed incremental plan, include config patch, and link a small sim harness for the qa team. tagging @ben @carla for review.
deploy-bot: scheduled: create rfc/000-prefetch-transport-negotiation.md in the proposals folder (assigned: alice) :white_check_mark:
alice: thanks — will iterate. :thumbsup:
